rule: Grant = PAL-CBOR map { body, sigEd25519, sigMldsa65 }; msg = ascii("pal3-grant-v1") || SHA-384(body); both signatures MUST verify with ML-DSA context "pal3-grant-v1". Rules checked on the decoded body: v = 1, requirePq = true, watermark = false (E_PAL3_GRANT_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRAINT otherwise), issuer keys of 32 and 1952 bytes, and a grant with expiresAtMs > 0 and expiresAtMs <= now is expired (E_PAL3_ACCESS_EXPIRED in grant.issue). Unknown map keys are ignored. All signatures are made in the deterministic ML-DSA mode.

objects.name: baselineIdentityGrant
objects.description: Read and list of one share for an identity, expires one hour after issue

objects.name: deviceGrantWithAllConstraints
objects.description: Device grant over a folder prefix with every constraint and one UTC time window

objects.name: anonymousListGrant
objects.description: Anonymous list of everything, no expiry (expiresAtMs = 0 means no limit)

objects.name: unknownKeyIsIgnored
objects.description: A grant body with an extra map key outside A.5 item 3: the signature covers it, the verifier accepts the grant and ignores the key

rejected.name: signatureCoversAnotherResource
rejected.description: The body names share:secret but the signatures were made over the body of share:docs

rejected.name: flippedEd25519Signature
rejected.description: One bit of the Ed25519 signature is flipped (strict-AND: the ML-DSA signature alone is not enough)

rejected.name: watermarkIsRefused
rejected.description: A signed grant with watermark = true: the constraint cannot be enforced, so the verifier refuses the whole grant (section 9)

rejected.name: requirePqFalse
rejected.description: requirePq is false: unsupported version or missing requirePq

rejected.name: expiredGrant
rejected.description: A correctly signed grant whose expiresAtMs is not after the receiver clock (nowMs): grant.issue refuses it with E_PAL3_ACCESS_EXPIRED
